answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. Consider a falcon as the anchor of the cost.
